text_block_list.name: Mejiro Palmer
text_block_list.text: Ardaaaan! Help us!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardan
text_block_list.text:
Goodness, if it isn't Palmer and Helios.
Hehe... Do
you both have another test?

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
You've got it! It's on the Edo period, I
think? But,
like, wow, this test is
difficult! You gotta help us
girlies out!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardan
text_block_list.text:
The Edo period, is it? Right then, let's
have some
fun studying for it with some
immersive
learning. ♪

text_block_list.name: Palmer and Helios
text_block_list.text: ...Huh?

text_block_list.name: Palmer and Helios
text_block_list.text: ...Why did we come to a hot spring?

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardan
text_block_list.text:
Hehe. Actually, we didn't come here for
the hot spring. This inn was founded
during the Edo
period, and they offer a
handicraft class.

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardan
text_block_list.text:
The class provides a unique opportunity to
immerse ourselves in Edo-era history
and culture, so let's learn today with
some hands-on
experience!

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text: Omigosh, this place was built in the Edo era? Now that's a vibe! I just know it's gonna be so hype!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Palmer
text_block_list.text:
Whoa, an immersive, hands-on class
sounds
awesome! Let's do it!

text_block_list.name: Inn Staff
text_block_list.text: The art of tsumami-zaiku dates back to the Edo period, during which it became extraordinarily popular. Today, we'll be using Edo-era techniques to create ornamental hairpins called kanzashi.

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Palmer
text_block_list.text:
Phew! I am just not cut out for this super
detailed
work! This sure is tough!

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
Yeah, I'm getting nowhere with mine
either! This
tsumami-zaiku thing is no
joke!

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
It's hard to believe careful work like
this can end
up making such fierce flowers,
though! Wearing something like this in
your hair is like the definition of drip!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardan
text_block_list.text:
Hehe. I suppose the Edo period itself
had a lot of
this "drip." After all...

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardan
text_block_list.text:
Kabuki theater as we know it was also
developed during the Edo period, and
the kabuki performers
were superstars to
the masses.

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardan
text_block_list.text:
Those kabuki performers were real
trendsetters in Edo society, and people
would copy the way they
dressed,
including their kanzashi.

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
Whoa, for real?! They were, like, the OG
models
and pop stars, then!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Palmer
text_block_list.text: Omigosh, does that mean fans repped their favorite kabuki actors by wearing cute little kanzashi? That sounds so fun!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardan
text_block_list.text:
That's right. They wore checkered
kimonos, which were in style at the time,
styled their obi the same way their
favorite performer did, and collected 
woodblock portraits of their favorite
actors.

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Palmer
text_block_list.text:
People used to copy their faves back
then too? I
totally get that!

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
Wait, you said checkered patterns were
the big thing back then, right? Ugh, that
is so fire! I wanna wear something with a
blue checkered
pattern too!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardan
text_block_list.text:
Soba stalls were also enormously
popular during that period. I wouldn't be
too surprised if people
even queued up
for them back then, you know.

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
Hey, that's just like how people line up
for pancakes at cafes now! Hahaha!
That's so funny!
They're not so different
from us, huh?

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardan
text_block_list.text:
The Edo period lasted just over 260
years and was a relatively peaceful time,
which is why popular culture among the
common people was
able to flourish.

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
Wooow. The lords back then must've
been
goated!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardan
text_block_list.text:
Quite right. The political system was well
organized and allowed for the
existence of feudal lords who supported
the elite and powerful shoguns. That's
what ensured the stability of the 
government.

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Palmer
text_block_list.text:
Ooh, it's starting to make sense! Hmm...
Wait, so the first shogun of the Edo era
was Ieyasu, right? So it's thanks to him
that society had such a major
glow-up!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Palmer
text_block_list.text:
That was so much fun! And I learned a
lot too! I
feel like I know all the deets
about the Edo
period now!

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
No kidding! Ardan, your teaching skills
are, like,
totally legit. We owe you one!

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
One day, I happen to see Mejiro Palmer
and
Daitaku Helios walking up to Mejiro
Palmer while
she's reading.

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
Listen to this, Ardan! We just got our
history test
scores back and we aaate! It
was all thanks to
you, queen! ☆

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Palmer
text_block_list.text:
And that hands-on crafting class we had
was so
fun. You've got me thinking
history might actually
be pretty cool!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardan
text_block_list.text:
Hehe, well... I'm just glad that I could
help.

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardan
text_block_list.text:
In fact, knowing that you two have taken
such an
interest in history has delighted
me to no end.
